findings.summary: Luna did not enumerate any current product or presentation despite claiming a 130-item Bethesda Row Toast catalog. The official site establishes six locations, while the endpoint is Bethesda Row only, so the 191 frozen dc-metro rows cannot receive a location-wide product reconciliation.
Luna omitted the official Catering HTML surface and the Google Drive Catering Menu PDF linked from official breakfast and lunch pages.

Luna's assertion that no restaurant-issued allergen evidence exists is incorrect. The official homepage gives limited dairy, peanut, tree-nut, egg/vegan, and gluten cross-contact statements. It remains incomplete and cannot validate item-level complete arrays or negatives.
The official homepage says gluten-free bagels cannot be guaranteed zero cross contamination. The frozen rows contain no item-level may-contain representation or source treatment for that warning.

The frozen file contains descriptive text, category labels, campaign/navigation text, and broad official-ingredients allergen arrays alongside products. Without the full current location-specific catalog and an ingredient matrix, assigning a common normalized-match disposition or complete allergen arrays is unsafe.

summary: Independent verification found material discrepancies: Luna omitted official catering surfaces and limited restaurant-issued allergen/cross-contact evidence, while also failing to enumerate any claimed Toast products or presentation IDs. The scope remains unresolved because the only claimed current ordering catalog is Bethesda Row, MD within a dc-metro restaurant record. All 191 frozen keys were reconciled once as location-mismatch/accurately-unavailable pending a complete, current location-specific catalog and authoritative item-level ingredient/allergen evidence; no negative or complete allergen claim is supported.
